# Physical eject, artwork and old UI diagnosis — October 18, 2026

## Evidence and what is actually known

**Owner photograph:** a blue-gradient `Safe to disconnect` screen, `NOT CONNECTED` badge, `Nothing to show yet` copy and blue legacy playback footer. This design is the *old renderer* and cannot be generated by `podthing-v0.1.0-test.14` source: test.14's `BuildView` and `Painter.Render` select only the dark unified UI even after eject. Therefore the photograph shows an older running application image, an older A/B firmware slot, or a flash that did not update the active image. Which of these occurred cannot be known from the photo alone. Test.14 is already published with successful firmware/boot CI; flashing must be confirmed by checking the **About -> Version**, downloadable `/api/state` `version`, or the new visible version label after eject. Do not paper over this with another cosmetic UI branch. A correctly flashed firmware must show the charcoal UI in all states.

**Filesystem eject vs iPod USB disconnect:** the owner saw a `Safe to disconnect` screen while the iPod still appeared connected. The earlier `Volume.Eject` only called Linux `umount(2)`. A successful unmount is data-safe, but **does not signal USB disconnection** or guarantee the iPod's own screen will exit its connected state. Source inspection proves there was no post-unmount USB release. This patch records those as separate stages.

**Album covers:** without a device report, the exact libgpod/ArtworkDB failure for the owner's specific albums is unknown, and the pictured post-eject screen cannot establish artwork behavior while mounted (post-eject clears all artwork on purpose). Independently verified source bugs: after a failed cover fetch `coverTried` blocked retries for the entire mount; the embedded fallback stopped at the first alternate album track even when it lacked artwork; and the libgpod worker had a sticky startup-error state with short initialization deadline. The worker's `NONE` response concealed whether ArtworkDB was absent, track ID mismatched, or a thumbnail was unavailable. These are fixed or diagnosed in this patch. Libgpod itself is documented to read iTunesDB *and* ArtworkDB in `itdb_parse()`; no direct evidence yet that the user's exact artwork formats are supported.

## Changes implemented

- **Post-unmount USB release:** `storage.Volume` remembers the precise iPod USB sysfs device that backed the mounted partition. After decoder/artwork-worker stop and a successful normal read-only unmount, the app checks that the same disk partition is still under the same **Apple USB device** and writes `0` only to that device's Linux `authorized` attribute. It never deauthorizes a whole host controller, another USB hub, or an unrelated Apple device. It refuses to run while mounted or on missing/mismatched identity. No forced unmount, fsck, USB reset, or iPod filesystem write. See Linux kernel's USB authorization reference: https://www.kernel.org/doc/html/v5.10/usb/authorization.html
- **Honest statuses:** if Linux can release the iPod USB device, it records that success. If release fails, the library is still safely unmounted, and the UI explicitly says the USB link may remain active. USB authorization is a **logical** detach, not VBUS power removal. Whether the stock Classic screen visibly returns to its music menu still needs physical verification.
- **Artwork robustness:** up to five tracks from one matching artist and album (the representative first) are tried for embedded artwork when ArtworkDB has no usable thumbnail. Failed covers can be retried after a thirty-second cooldown. libgpod startup has a thirty-second limit for large libraries; transient worker errors can restart after backoff. Output log identifies missing ArtworkDB, missing libgpod track-ID match, missing thumbnail, or PNG/save errors. Successful cover source logged for first covers. Album images are genuine; no invented artwork or writes to the iPod.
- **Firmware revision:** the uniform dark Eject completion screen includes the application version, making an obsolete flashed slot apparent from a photo.

## Real-hardware acceptance test — do in this order

1. Verify the flashed build in Settings -> About -> Version or `GET /api/state`. Do **not** treat GitHub's latest release as proof the Car Thing is running it. On the new unified build, after Eject the screen must remain charcoal/dark and display `Firmware 0.1.0-test.N`.
2. With the known stock iPod attached through the existing powered USB host cable, confirm `Open iPod music (read-only)` reads the library. Previous host-mode reports have sometimes shown only Linux root hubs; no artwork or library code will work until Apple USB device enumeration is real.
3. Navigate to Albums; wait for asynchronous covers. On failure, select **Save diagnostics**, then obtain `/api/report` during host mode, or the saved report via recovery `http://10.42.1.2:8787/api/report/saved`. Look for `ARTWORK:` lines and worker stderr. Do not guess whether a missing image is caused by `ArtworkDB`, libgpod, embedded tags or track IDs.
4. Start playback through an actually detected USB DAC, then press top-bar Eject. Confirm the decoder is stopped, read-only mount is gone, and the host reports either `EJECT: ... released from Linux USB device authorization` or a precise failure. Only after the normal unmount has succeeded should PodThing attempt USB release.
5. Observe the iPod's own display. Even a successful Linux logical deauthorization is not proof the iPod firmware will clear its screen; if it does not, record that exact distinction in the bug report.
6. After any eject, unplug/replug the iPod to re-establish a fresh Linux-authorized USB session. This is expected after device deauthorization.

No code-only test can establish successful physical eject on a stock Classic, and the artwork root cause requires an actual device report. Keep the standalone firmware release gated on Go/race, Python and full ARM64 firmware/QEMU smoke CI.
